answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making each identity earn trust through a costly, verifiable work history, not by claiming it. A new agent starts at a jetty with no privileges: it must complete small, peer-graded tasks whose results are recorded in a shared kernel ledger. Only after a consistent record does it gain larger jobs or payments, like a jade seal earned rather than bought. Creating thousands of fakes then costs thousands of separate histories, and abandoning a caught identity loses all its work.
